inline_comments.comment: `showPanel` is declared `async` but no longer contains any `await` expression — the `focusOnUIElement` call is now fire-and-forget. The `async` keyword is dead weight: it wraps the return value in a resolved `Promise<void>` unnecessarily and signals to readers that something is being awaited when nothing is. Either drop `async` entirely, or (if the `Consumer`/`menuMapper` type requires a `Promise`-returning function) add a comment explaining that constraint. The same issue exists in `menu.tsx`'s `showSidebar`.
Same as the note in `addons.tsx`: `showSidebar` is marked `async` but contains no `await`. Remove `async` or document why the Promise return type is required.

On the `onClick` path, `showPanel(false)` is called, which triggers `api.focusOnUIElement(focusableUIElements.addonPanel, { forceFocus: false, poll: true })`. The `addonPanel` element (`storybook-panel-region`) is an `<aside>` / landmark div that is not natively focusable. With `forceFocus: false`, the browser will not focus it, so the polling loop will retry every 50 ms and time out after 500 ms on every button click — doing no useful work. Previously, the click path used `forceFocus: true` and always succeeded on the first poll. Consider skipping the `focusOnUIElement` call entirely when `forceFocus` is `false` (i.e., restructure `showPanel` to only call `focusOnUIElement` in the `forceFocus === true` branch), or remove the `poll: true` option so it returns immediately on failure. The same applies to `menu.tsx`'s `showSidebar`.

`focusOnUIElement` with `poll: true` returns a `Promise<boolean>`. The return value is silently discarded here (and at the corresponding `wasNavShown` block). This is fine functionally since we don't need the result, but it would be clearer to add a `void` prefix (`void fullAPI.focusOnUIElement(...)`) to signal the intentional discard and avoid a no-floating-promises lint warning.

general_comments.comment: This PR changes the click behavior of both the 'Show addon panel' and 'Show sidebar' toolbar buttons: previously a mouse click moved keyboard focus to the newly-revealed panel/sidebar region (the old code hardcoded `forceFocus: true` regardless of how `showPanel`/`showSidebar` was called); now a click leaves focus on the button. The PR description calls this intentional ('clicks focus controls'), but it is a potentially user-facing regression for people who mix mouse and keyboard navigation and expect focus to follow the newly revealed content. The change is worth a dedicated accessibility QA step — in particular, verify behavior with a screen reader (VoiceOver / NVDA) to confirm the change aligns with ARIA best practices for disclosure widgets, where focus is typically moved into the revealed region.

The animated landmark indicator (`useRegionFocusAnimation`) has been removed from both `addons.tsx` and `menu.tsx` with no replacement. The animation (2 px colored border, 1500 ms, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`) provided an explicit visual cue to low-vision users about which region gained focus. The PR description notes this is intentional, but it would be worth documenting in a comment or issue why the animation was dropped — particularly since the `useLandmarkIndicator` hook that powers F6/Shift+F6 landmark navigation still uses the same animation. Without that context, a future developer might re-add the animation to be consistent with the F6 path.
